name: Garamantian Wars
description: Series of Roman expeditions and clashes against the Saharan Garamantes kingdom, opening trans-Saharan contact with the future Sahel.

name: Wagadu (Ghana) Foundation Wars
description: Soninke consolidation of the Wagadu polity (Ghana Empire) over Aoukar through conquest of neighbouring clan polities in the late first millennium.

name: Takrur Foundation Conflicts
description: Early state formation along the Senegal River that produced the kingdom of Takrur, attested in Arabic sources from the ninth century.

name: Almoravid–Awdaghust Campaign
description: Almoravid seizure of the Saharan trade terminus Awdaghust from Ghanaian overlordship, opening the southern phase of the Almoravid expansion.

name: Sosso–Mandinka War (Kirina)
description: Sundiata Keita's defeat of Soumaoro Kanté of Sosso at Kirina, founding the Mali Empire.

name: Mali–Sosso Wars
description: Conflicts between Sundiata's Mande coalition and the Sosso of Soumaoro Kanté culminating in the destruction of Sosso power.

name: Sakura's Reconquest of Songhai
description: Mansa Sakura's campaigns reasserting Malian control over Gao and the middle Niger.

name: Mansa Musa's Conquest of Gao
description: General Saran Mandian's seizure of Gao for Mansa Musa on his return from the Mecca pilgrimage, bringing Songhai under Mali.

name: Mossi Raids on Timbuktu
description: Recurring Mossi cavalry raids from the Volta basin into the Niger Bend cities, including the 1330 sack of Timbuktu under Nasaré.

name: Mali Civil War of Succession (1360s)
description: Dynastic struggles after the death of Mansa Suleyman that weakened central Malian authority.

name: Tuareg Capture of Timbuktu (1433)
description: Maghsharen Tuareg under Akil ag Malwal seized Timbuktu from Mali, ending direct Malian control of the city.

name: Sonni Ali's Conquests
description: Sonni Ali Ber's campaigns building the Songhai Empire, including the capture of Timbuktu (1468), seven-year siege of Jenne, and wars against the Mossi.

name: Siege of Jenne (1473)
description: Sonni Ali's prolonged blockade of Jenne ending in the city's submission to Songhai.

name: Battle of Tondibi
description: Moroccan arquebusiers under Judar Pasha destroyed the Songhai army, ending the Songhai Empire.

name: Saadian Invasion of Songhai
description: Sultan Ahmad al-Mansur's trans-Saharan invasion that toppled Songhai and established the Pashalik of Timbuktu.

name: Askia Muhammad's Wars
description: Askia Muhammad I's campaigns extending Songhai control over Air, Hausaland, the Mossi, and Diara, including the 1497–98 jihad against the Mossi.

name: Songhai Civil War (1582–1591)
description: Succession struggles among Askia descendants that fatally weakened Songhai before the Moroccan invasion.

name: Battle of Anfao
description: Askia Muhammad's victory over Sonni Baru that secured Askia's seizure of the Songhai throne.

name: Kebbi–Songhai War
description: Kanta Kotal's revolt against Askia Muhammad founded the kingdom of Kebbi and broke Songhai control of Hausaland's western marches.

name: Kanem–Bornu Civil War
description: Long Sefuwa–Bulala dynastic conflict that drove the Kanem capital from Njimi to Ngazargamu west of Lake Chad.

name: Idris Alooma's Wars
description: Mai Idris Alooma's musket-equipped campaigns that restored Bornu hegemony over Kanem and the Lake Chad basin.

name: Kano–Katsina Wars
description: Two centuries of intermittent war between the rival Hausa city-states of Kano and Katsina over trade routes and tribute.

name: Queen Amina's Conquests
description: Queen Amina of Zazzau's wars expanding Zaria's reach south to the Niger and east into Kano's sphere.

name: Jukun (Kwararafa) Wars
description: Kwararafa raids and invasions of Hausaland and Bornu from the Benue valley in the seventeenth century, including the 1671 sack of Kano.

name: Bornu–Sokoto Wars
description: Wars between al-Kanemi's Bornu and the Fulani jihadist Sokoto Caliphate that contained the jihad's eastern expansion.

name: Wadai–Bornu Wars
description: Recurrent nineteenth-century wars between the Sultanate of Wadai and Bornu over Kanem and the Lake Chad basin.

name: Rabih's Wars
description: Rabih az-Zubayr's Sudanese slave-army conquests across Wadai and Bornu, ended by the French at the Battle of Kousséri.

name: Battle of Kousséri
description: Three converging French columns defeated and killed Rabih az-Zubayr, completing French conquest of the Lake Chad basin.

name: Voulet–Chanoine Mission
description: French Central African Mission across the Sahel marked by the massacres at Birni-N'Konni and Zinder before the officers were killed by their own troops.

name: Mai Ali Ghaji's Restoration of Bornu
description: Mai Ali Ghaji ibn Dunama's campaigns founding the new Bornu capital at Ngazargamu and restoring Sefuwa power over the Bulala.

name: Borgu Wars
description: Centuries of Borgu resistance to Songhai, Nupe, and Oyo, most famously the defeat of Oyo at the Battle of Olokomeji.

name: Nupe Wars
description: Long arc of Nupe wars from Tsoede's foundation through Oyo invasions, internal succession wars, the Fulani jihad, and British conquest of Bida.

name: Oyo Conquest of Dahomey
description: Repeated Oyo cavalry invasions that reduced Dahomey to tributary status under Agaja and Tegbesu.

name: Dahomey Conquest of Whydah
description: King Agaja's conquest and destruction of the slave-trading kingdom of Hueda, giving Dahomey direct access to the Atlantic.

name: Dahomey Conquest of Allada
description: Agaja's seizure of Allada that brought Dahomey to the coastal slave-trade circuit.

name: Asante–Denkyira War
description: Osei Tutu and Okomfo Anokye's victory at Feyiase that founded Asante independence from Denkyira.

name: Asante–Akyem Wars
description: Asante campaigns against the Akyem and Akwamu that extended Asante power to the coast hinterland.

name: Akwamu Conquest of Accra
description: Akwamu's seizure of Great Accra and the Ga coast, consolidating its grip on the Gold Coast trade.

name: Komenda Wars
description: Anglo-Dutch-Eguafo wars over the Komenda coast that established English supremacy in the central Gold Coast.

name: Fante–Asante Wars
description: Asante invasions of the Fante coast that prefigured the Anglo-Asante wars.

name: Battle of Nsamankow
description: Asante victory over British forces that killed Governor Charles MacCarthy.

name: Battle of Katamanso
description: British-allied coastal coalition defeated Asante at Katamanso, ending the first phase of Asante expansion south.

name: Sagrenti War (Third Anglo-Ashanti War)
description: Garnet Wolseley's expedition to Kumasi that burned the Asante capital.

name: Yaa Asantewaa War
description: Asante uprising led by Queen Mother Yaa Asantewaa against British demands for the Golden Stool, ending in Asante's annexation.

name: First Franco-Dahomean War
description: French defence of Cotonou and Porto-Novo against King Béhanzin of Dahomey.

name: Second Franco-Dahomean War
description: Colonel Dodds's columns broke the Dahomey army of King Béhanzin and annexed the kingdom to France.

name: Franco-Mandingo Wars
description: Wars between France and Samori Touré's Wassoulou Empire, ending with Samori's capture in 1898.

name: Battle of Woyowayanko
description: First major French clash with Samori Touré's forces on the upper Niger.

name: Siege of Sikasso (1887–88)
description: Samori Touré's failed siege of Tieba Traoré's tata at Sikasso.

name: French Conquest of Sikasso (1898)
description: French storming of Babemba Traoré's fortress at Sikasso, ending the Kénédougou kingdom.

name: Toucouleur Wars (Umarian Jihad)
description: Al-Hajj Umar Tall's jihad sweeping the western Sudan from Futa Toro across Kaarta, Segou, and Macina.

name: Siege of Medine
description: Faidherbe's relief of the French fort at Medine halted Umar Tall's drive on the Senegal valley.

name: Battle of Segou
description: Umar Tall's capture of Segou ended the Bambara Empire of Segou.

name: Battle of Hamdullahi
description: Umar Tall destroyed Ahmadu III's Macina Empire and took Hamdullahi, the Fulani jihadist capital.

name: Battle of Deguembéré
description: Umar Tall's death in a cave near Bandiagara during a Macina-Fulani revolt against Toucouleur rule.

name: French Conquest of the Toucouleur Empire
description: Colonels Archinard and Combes's campaigns against Ahmadu Tall taking Segou, Nioro, and Bandiagara.

name: Macina Jihad
description: Seku Amadu's Fulani jihad founding the Macina Empire after victories over the Bambara and Arma at Noukouma.

name: Battle of Noukouma
description: Seku Amadu's victory over the Bambara of Segou that founded the Macina jihad state.

name: Futa Jallon Jihad
description: Karamokho Alfa and Ibrahim Sori's Fulani jihad that founded the Imamate of Futa Jallon in the Guinea highlands.

name: Battle of Talansan
description: Inaugural victory of the Futa Jallon jihad over the animist Sosoe.

name: Futa Toro Jihad
description: Suleyman Bal and Abdul Kader's torodbe revolution overthrowing the Denanke and founding the Imamate of Futa Toro.

name: Bondu Jihad
description: Malik Sy's foundation of the Muslim state of Bondu through war against the Malinke chiefs of the upper Gambia.

name: Soninke–Marabout Wars
description: Long Muslim-pagan civil wars across Senegambia from Maba Diakhou Bâ's jihad to the fall of Fodé Kaba.

name: Maba Diakhou's Jihad
description: Maba Diakhou Bâ's Muslim jihad in the Saloum and Rip, ending at the Battle of Somb where the Sine king Maad a Sinig Coumba Ndoffene Famak Joof killed him.

name: Battle of Somb
description: Serer king Coumba Ndoffene Famak's victory over the marabout army of Maba Diakhou at Fandane-Thiouthioune.

name: Lat Dior's Resistance
description: Damel Lat Dior Ngoné Latyr Diop's wars against the French in Cayor, ending at the Battle of Dékheulé.

name: Battle of Dékheulé
description: French defeat of Lat Dior at Dékheulé, killing the Damel and ending Cayor's independence.

name: Hubbu Movement
description: Mamadou Juhe's egalitarian Muslim revolt against the aristocracy of the Futa Jallon, crushed by Samori Touré.

name: Owu War
description: Destruction of the Yoruba town of Owu by an Ife–Ijebu coalition, opening the cycle of Yoruba civil wars.

name: Yoruba Civil Wars
description: Umbrella for the century of inter-Yoruba conflict that destroyed Old Oyo and produced Ibadan, Abeokuta, and the Ekitiparapo confederation.

name: Fall of Old Oyo (Oyo–Ilorin War)
description: Afonja's revolt and the Fulani-led conquest of Ilorin that destroyed Old Oyo and triggered the Yoruba migrations south.

name: Battle of Osogbo
description: Ibadan's defeat of Ilorin halted Sokoto's southward jihad into Yorubaland.

name: Ijaye War
description: Ibadan–Ijaye war that destroyed Kurunmi's town of Ijaye and confirmed Ibadan as the dominant Yoruba power.

name: Kiriji War (Ekitiparapo)
description: Sixteen-year stalemate between Ibadan and the Ekitiparapo coalition that ended in British-brokered peace and the absorption of Yorubaland into Lagos Colony.

name: Egba–Dahomey Wars
description: Dahomean invasions of Abeokuta repelled by the Egba at the celebrated battles of 1851 and 1864.

name: Battle of Abeokuta (1851)
description: Egba defeat of Ghezo's Dahomean invasion at Abeokuta.

name: Bombardment of Lagos
description: Royal Navy bombardment that deposed Oba Kosoko and installed Akitoye, paving the way for British annexation of Lagos.

name: British Annexation of Lagos
description: Cession of Lagos by Oba Dosunmu under British naval pressure, founding the Lagos Colony.

name: Sokoto Jihad of Usman dan Fodio
description: Usman dan Fodio's Fulani jihad overthrowing the Hausa kingdoms and founding the Sokoto Caliphate.

name: Battle of Tsuntua
description: Heavy defeat of Usman dan Fodio's followers by Yunfa's Gobir army early in the Sokoto jihad.

name: Battle of Tabkin Kwatto
description: Usman dan Fodio's first decisive battlefield victory over Gobir launched the conquest of Hausaland.

name: Bornu Resistance to the Sokoto Jihad
description: Muhammad al-Kanemi's mobilization that drove Sokoto forces out of Bornu and re-founded the Bornu state at Kukawa.

name: Adamawa Jihad
description: Modibo Adama's Fulani jihad extending Sokoto authority into northern Cameroon and the Benue valley.

name: Hadejia Rebellion
description: Buhari dan Umaru's long revolt against the Sokoto Caliphate from Hadejia.

name: Kano Civil War
description: Basasa succession war in Kano on the eve of British conquest.

name: Anglo-Sokoto War
description: Frederick Lugard's campaigns capturing Kano and Sokoto and killing Caliph Attahiru I at the Battle of Burmi.

name: Battle of Burmi
description: Final stand of Caliph Attahiru I against British forces after the fall of Sokoto.

name: Satiru Revolt
description: Mahdist uprising at Satiru crushed jointly by British and Caliphate forces.

name: Kaarta Wars
description: Long arc of Massassi Bambara wars from Kaarta's foundation through its destruction by Umar Tall in 1854.

name: Bambara Empire of Segou Wars
description: Mamari Coulibaly's foundation wars and the Segou Bambara's later conflicts with Macina, Kaarta, and Umar Tall.

name: Kong Empire Wars
description: Wars of Sékou Watara's Dyula Kong empire from its foundation through its destruction by Samori Touré in 1897.

name: Samori's Destruction of Kong
description: Samori Touré's sack of Kong on the eve of his French capture.

name: Mossi–Songhai Wars
description: Sonni Ali's and Askia Muhammad's campaigns against the Mossi, including Askia's 1497 jihad declared against Naaba Nasere.

name: French Conquest of the Mossi
description: Voulet and Cazemajou's columns captured Ouagadougou and ended Mogho Naaba Wobogo's independence.

name: Volta–Bani War
description: Mass anti-French uprising in present-day Burkina Faso and Mali during the First World War.

name: Kaocen Revolt
description: Sanusi-backed Tuareg uprising in the Aïr mountains besieging the French garrison at Agadez.

name: Adrar Campaign (Mauritania)
description: French conquest of the Mauritanian Adrar under Colonel Gouraud, ending the emirate's independence.

name: Pacification of Mauritania
description: Long French campaign subduing the Trarza, Brakna, Adrar, and Hodh emirates of Mauritania.

name: Hut Tax War
description: Temne and Mende uprising against the British hut tax led by Bai Bureh.

name: Asante–Gyaman Wars
description: Asante wars subjugating the Gyaman kingdom across what is now Côte d'Ivoire and northern Ghana.

name: Asante–Dagomba War
description: Opoku Ware's invasion of Dagbon that subjected Yendi to Asante tribute.

name: Egba Revolt (Fall of Old Oyo Vassals)
description: Lisabi's revolt and the Egba refoundation at Abeokuta out of the wreck of Oyo.

name: Anglo-Aro War
description: British expedition that destroyed the Aro Long Juju and broke the Aro Confederacy.

name: Ekumeku Movement
description: Anioma Igbo guerrilla resistance to the Royal Niger Company and British colonial authority west of the Niger.

name: Anglo-Egba War
description: British military suppression of the Egba United Government, ending Abeokuta's de facto autonomy.

name: Adubi War
description: Egba tax revolt against indirect-rule chiefs and the colonial government.

name: Aba Women's War
description: Mass women's uprising in southeastern Nigeria against warrant chiefs and colonial taxation.

name: Bai Bureh's War
description: Bai Bureh's Temne guerrilla campaign forming the northern theatre of the Hut Tax War.

name: Liberian–Grebo War
description: Series of Liberian wars subduing the Grebo of Cape Palmas.

name: Kru Wars
description: Liberian government campaign against the Kru of the Sasstown coast, supported by U.S. naval landings.

name: Kamerun Campaign
description: Allied conquest of German Kamerun in the First World War.

name: Togoland Campaign
description: British–French conquest of German Togoland in August 1914.

name: Bafut Wars
description: German colonial wars against Fon Abumbi I of Bafut in the Cameroonian Grassfields.

name: Nso–German War
description: German conquest of the Nso kingdom in the Cameroonian Grassfields.

name: Anglo-Ijebu War
description: Maxim-gun rout of the Ijebu army at Imagbon, opening the interior of Yorubaland to British power.

name: Mahdist Movement in Hausaland (Hayatu)
description: Hayatu ibn Sa'id's Mahdist preaching and his alliance and war with Rabih in northern Adamawa.

name: First Tuareg Rebellion (Mali)
description: First post-independence Tuareg uprising in northern Mali, suppressed by the Keïta government.

name: Second Tuareg Rebellion
description: Tuareg uprisings in Mali and Niger ending in the National Pact (1992) and Ouagadougou Accord (1995).

name: Third Tuareg Rebellion (Niger 2007–09)
description: MNJ-led Tuareg uprising in northern Niger over uranium revenues and autonomy.

name: Northern Mali Conflict (2012– )
description: MNLA-Tuareg and jihadist rebellion that triggered French Operation Serval and now Wagner-backed counter-insurgency.

name: Operation Serval
description: French intervention halting the jihadist advance on Bamako and recapturing the northern Malian cities.

name: Operation Barkhane
description: French-led counter-terrorism operation across the G5 Sahel succeeding Serval, ending after the 2021–22 Bamako coups.

name: Battle of Konna
description: Jihadist capture and French recapture of Konna that triggered Operation Serval.

name: Western Sahara War (Mauritania theatre)
description: Mauritanian phase of the Western Sahara war, ending with Mauritania's withdrawal from Tiris al-Gharbiya.

name: Senegal–Mauritania Border War
description: Communal pogroms and expulsions along the Senegal River following clashes between Mauritanian Moors and Senegalese farmers.

name: PAIGC Insurgency in Portuguese Guinea
description: Amílcar Cabral's PAIGC liberation war that ended Portuguese rule in Guinea-Bissau and Cape Verde.

name: Cameroon UPC Insurgency
description: UPC-led Bamileke and Bassa insurgency against France and the Ahidjo government, sometimes called the Bamileke War.

name: Maitatsine Riots
description: Series of millenarian uprisings in northern Nigeria under Muhammadu Marwa Maitatsine that killed thousands.

name: Boko Haram Insurgency
description: Jihadist insurgency by Boko Haram and its ISWAP splinter across the Lake Chad basin.

name: Chibok Schoolgirls Kidnapping Operations
description: Boko Haram mass abduction at Chibok that internationalised the Lake Chad insurgency.

name: Niger Delta Conflict
description: Insurgency by MEND and successor groups over oil revenues and environmental destruction in the Niger Delta.

name: Ogoni Crisis
description: MOSOP-led Ogoni protests and military repression culminating in the execution of Ken Saro-Wiwa.

name: Nigerian Sharia Riots
description: Inter-religious riots in northern Nigeria over the extension of Sharia criminal law.

name: Plateau State Crisis
description: Recurring Christian–Muslim and Berom–Fulani communal violence around Jos.

name: Nigerian Bandit Conflict (North-West)
description: Armed-bandit and Fulani militia conflict across the Nigerian north-west.

name: Nigerian Farmer–Herder Conflict
description: Long-running Fulani herder–farmer violence across Nigeria's Middle Belt.

name: Mali 1968 Coup
description: Military overthrow of Modibo Keïta by Moussa Traoré.

name: 2012 Malian Coup
description: Sanogo-led mutiny that overthrew Amadou Toumani Touré as the north fell to MNLA and jihadists.

name: 2020 Malian Coup
description: Colonel Assimi Goïta's overthrow of Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta, beginning the Sahel coup wave.

name: 2022 Burkina Faso Coups
description: Twin coups by Damiba and Traoré amid worsening jihadist violence in the country's north and east.

name: 2023 Nigerien Coup
description: Presidential Guard general Tchiani's overthrow of Mohamed Bazoum, deepening the Sahel security crisis.

name: Burkinabé Insurgency
description: JNIM and ISGS insurgency that has displaced millions and now controls large parts of rural Burkina Faso.

name: First Ivorian Civil War
description: MPCI rebellion that split Côte d'Ivoire and triggered Opération Licorne and UN intervention.

name: Second Ivorian Civil War
description: Post-election war between forces loyal to Laurent Gbagbo and Alassane Ouattara, ended by French and UN intervention.

name: Bakassi Conflict
description: Nigeria–Cameroon border dispute and intermittent fighting over the Bakassi peninsula, resolved by the ICJ.

name: Mali–Burkina Faso Border War (Agacher Strip)
description: Brief Christmas War between Mali and Sankara's Burkina Faso over the mineral-rich Agacher Strip.

name: Toyota War
description: Final phase of the Chadian–Libyan war, where Chad's pickup-mounted forces routed Libya from the Aouzou Strip.

name: Chadian–Libyan War
description: Long Chadian–Libyan war over the Aouzou Strip, decided by the 1987 Toyota War.

name: FROLINAT Insurgency
description: Sahel–Saharan rebellion that opened the long Chadian Civil War.

name: Battle of N'Djamena (1980)
description: Battles between Hissène Habré and Goukouni Oueddei's factions for control of the Chadian capital.

name: Chadian Civil War (2005–10)
description: Sudanese-backed rebel campaigns against Idriss Déby including the Battle of N'Djamena (2008).

name: Tibu–Arab Conflict in Chad
description: Tubu mining and inter-communal violence in the Tibesti and the Chadian north.

name: Cameroonian Anglophone Crisis
description: Armed conflict between the Cameroonian government and Ambazonian separatists in the country's English-speaking regions.

name: Boko Haram Insurgency in Cameroon
description: Boko Haram cross-border attacks and Cameroonian counter-insurgency in the Far North Region.

name: Lord's Resistance Army in CAR–Chad–Cameroon
description: Spillover LRA attacks into eastern Cameroon and southern Chad as the group dispersed from northern Uganda.

name: Diffa Insurgency
description: Boko Haram and ISWAP attacks on Niger's Diffa region around Lake Chad.

name: Tillabéri Insurgency
description: ISGS and JNIM violence across Niger's western Tillabéri region.

name: Casamance Conflict
description: Low-intensity MFDC separatist insurgency in southern Senegal.

name: ECOMOG Intervention in Liberia
description: ECOWAS's first peace-enforcement deployment, fighting Charles Taylor's NPFL during the First Liberian Civil War.

name: Liberian Coup of 1980
description: Samuel Doe's overthrow of William Tolbert, ending 133 years of Americo-Liberian rule.

name: Battle for Freetown (1999)
description: RUF/AFRC offensive on Freetown known as Operation No Living Thing, the bloodiest episode of the Sierra Leonean civil war.

name: Operation Palliser
description: British intervention that stabilised the Sierra Leonean government and broke the RUF advance.

name: Guinean Border Clashes (2000–01)
description: RUF and Liberian incursions into south-eastern Guinea repulsed by the Guinean army with Western support.

name: Movement for Democracy in Liberia (LURD/MODEL)
description: LURD and MODEL offensives that toppled Charles Taylor in the Second Liberian Civil War.

name: Operation Licorne
description: French peacekeeping operation in Côte d'Ivoire spanning both civil wars.

name: Battle of Abidjan (2011)
description: Final battle of the Second Ivorian Civil War ending in the capture of Laurent Gbagbo.

name: Guinea Coups and Bloody Monday
description: Captain Camara's coup and the 2009 Conakry stadium massacre during the post-Conté transition.

name: Operation Eagle Claw (MNJTF)
description: Lake Chad Basin Commission–led counter-Boko Haram task force operating from Lake Chad headquarters.

name: Nasir al-Din's Jihad
description: Awbek Ashfaga (Nasir al-Din)'s Berber Toubenan jihad against Wolof and Fulani rulers of the lower Senegal.

name: Wolof–French Wars
description: Recurring wars between French Saint-Louis and the Wolof kingdoms of Cayor, Baol, Jolof, and Waalo.

name: Battle of Médina (Faidherbe)
description: Faidherbe's annexation of Waalo, the first French conquest of an interior Senegalese kingdom.

name: Faidherbe Wars
description: Governor Faidherbe's campaigns expanding French Senegal from Saint-Louis into the interior.

name: Sefuwa–Bulala Wars
description: Civil wars that drove the Sefuwa dynasty out of Kanem to refound at Ngazargamu.

name: Damagaram Wars
description: Foundation and expansion wars of the Sultanate of Damagaram around Zinder, ending with French conquest.

name: Battle of Adwa-style Defeat: Sokoto–Kebbi War (Argungu)
description: Wars between the Sokoto Caliphate and the rump Kebbi state at Argungu.

name: Anglo-Sokoto Conquest of Bida
description: Royal Niger Company defeat of Emir Abubakar of Bida, the first major British conquest of a Sokoto emirate.

name: Conquest of Ilorin
description: Royal Niger Company campaign under George Goldie that captured Ilorin from the Sokoto Caliphate.

name: Songhai–Mossi War of 1483
description: Sonni Ali's repulse of a Mossi raid on Walata and his retaliatory invasion of Yatenga.

name: Songhai Conquest of Air
description: Askia Muhammad's conquest of Agadez and the Aïr massif.

name: Akan–Akwamu Expansion Wars
description: Akwamu's century of conquests creating a coastal empire from the Volta to Whydah before its destruction in 1730.

name: Fall of Akwamu
description: Akyem-led coalition that destroyed Akwamu and broke its coastal empire.

name: Asante–Banda War
description: Asante destruction of the Banda kingdom in northern Ghana.

name: Bonduku War (Asante–Abron)
description: Osei Bonsu's reconquest of Gyaman and capture of Adinkra of Bonduku.

name: Benin–Itsekiri Wars
description: Wars between Benin and its breakaway Itsekiri kingdom of Warri.

name: Punitive Expedition against Benin
description: British naval expedition that sacked Benin City and ended the Benin Empire after the Phillips massacre.

name: Brass Oil War (Akassa Raid)
description: King Koko of Nembe's attack on the Royal Niger Company station at Akassa.

name: Borno–Wadai War of the Mahdists
description: Rabih's destruction of the Bornu army at Gashagar and seizure of Kukawa.

name: First Mali–Burkina War (1974)
description: Brief 1974 clash between Mali and Upper Volta over the Agacher Strip, predecessor to the 1985 Christmas War.

name: Gambian Coup Attempt of 1981
description: Failed leftist coup against Jawara crushed by Senegalese intervention, leading to the short-lived Senegambia Confederation.

name: Sierra Leone 1997 AFRC Coup
description: Major Johnny Paul Koroma's AFRC coup that joined the RUF and prolonged the Sierra Leonean civil war.

name: Mali 1991 Revolution
description: Mass protests and Touré-led coup that overthrew Moussa Traoré.

name: 1987 Burkinabé Coup
description: Blaise Compaoré's overthrow and killing of Thomas Sankara.

name: Liberian Plot of Quiwonkpa (1985)
description: General Thomas Quiwonkpa's failed coup against Samuel Doe and the subsequent ethnic reprisals against the Gio and Mano.

name: Pashalik of Timbuktu Wars
description: Wars of the Arma successor state of the Saadians defending Timbuktu against Tuareg, Mossi, Bambara, and Fulani.

name: Wolof Civil Wars (Battle of Danki)
description: Amari Ngoné Sobel Fall's victory at the Battle of Danki that broke up the Jolof Empire.

name: Jolof–Cayor War
description: Cayor and Baol's breakaway wars that destroyed the Jolof Empire's hegemony over Senegal.

name: Cape Verdean War of Independence
description: Cape Verdean theatre of the PAIGC liberation war, achieving independence in 1975.

name: Songhai–Borgu War
description: Askia Muhammad's failed invasion of Borgu, one of his rare reverses.

name: Battle of Olokomeji
description: Borgu defeat of an Oyo invasion that began the decline of Oyo's northern hegemony.

name: Oyo Civil War (Gaha's Reign and Fall)
description: Basorun Gaha's tyranny and his overthrow by Alaafin Abiodun that prefigured Oyo's nineteenth-century collapse.

name: Asante Conquest of Tekyiman
description: Opoku Ware's destruction of Bono-Manso and absorption of Tekyiman.

name: Battle of Kalumfardo
description: Rabih's victory over Hashim al-Kanemi's Bornu army that opened the way to Kukawa.

name: Kaabu–Futa Jallon Wars (Battle of Kansala)
description: Futa Jallon's destruction of the Mandinka empire of Kaabu at the Battle of Kansala (Turban Keloo).

name: Kaabu Empire Wars
description: Mandinka empire of Kaabu's wars from independence from Mali to its destruction at Kansala.

name: British Conquest of Northern Ghana
description: British campaigns establishing the Northern Territories of the Gold Coast in the wake of the fall of Asante.
